steps.title: Identify the representation being mapped
steps.explanation: This view maps an artistic graph to a rendered surface. It can establish a neutral pose and stable topology; it contains no tissue degrees of freedom or transpose force-transfer operator. The equations below concern additional mechanical mappings.
steps.observe: A neutral mannequin is shown. The state has no force, pressure or contact output to transfer.

steps.title: Check the simplest motion transfer
steps.explanation: Move the entire character by 0.4 scene units. The render surface follows the root once, without changing the local pose. This is a useful rigid-placement check; it does not test the chapter’s proposed residual tissue embedding, which is not present in the poser.
steps.observe: The character translates as one object. No added tissue displacement, deformation energy or reaction force is claimed.

steps.title: Separate visual following from contact mechanics
steps.explanation: Prescribe the hand near the torso and inspect the interface. The skin follows the graph, but the torso does not push back through a tissue-to-bone force map. The paddle/block and weighted-cylinder exercises below remain separate, unfinished mechanical demonstrations.
steps.observe: The arm reaches the prescribed target. There is no two-way tissue reaction, sliding model or contact-pressure readout.

audit.finding: The generic poser could be mistaken for implementation of the chapter’s skinning-collapse or two-way interface exercises.
audit.change: The sequence explicitly tests geometric reference/placement/following and states which mechanical exercises are still missing.
audit.remaining: Weighted-cylinder LBS distortion, the two-way paddle/block exercise, residual tissue embedding and interface work checks remain unimplemented here.
